metadata.title: Know Eminem From My View
metadata.author: Your Name
metadata.description: A digital diary of emotional moments

pages.text: I was 14 when I first heard 'The Real Slim Shady'. I didn't understand all the words, but I felt something. A voice that didn't care about being liked. That mattered to me.
Unlike other rappers, he didn't rap about being untouchable. He rapped about being broken. About the struggle. That's when I realized—this isn't just music. It's therapy.
By college, his albums were my soundtrack to survival. Every breakup, every doubt, every 'I can't do this'—he had a song that made me feel less alone.
